title: logins.v1
description:
Failed sign-ins to the site's control panel, as counts. An allowlist: anything absent is rejected, not ignored.

Note what is not here, and why. There is no username, no email address, no user id, no source address and no per-attempt record — only totals. A stream of 'who tried to sign in as whom, from where' is a log of real people's behaviour on somebody else's website, and forwarding it to a monitoring platform would be collection this product has no stated purpose for. What an operator needs is whether a site is being attacked and whether anybody is locked out, and both are numbers.

One caveat travels with these figures and is repeated in the interface: Craft resets a user's failed-attempt counter on a successful sign-in, so a total here is a floor rather than a count of everything that has ever been tried.

window_hours.description: How far back the counts reach. Bounded, because an unbounded window would make every number monotonic and therefore meaningless.

failed_attempts.description: Sum of outstanding failed-attempt counters across accounts whose last failure falls inside the window.

accounts_locked.description: Accounts Craft has locked out. The number that most often needs a person, because somebody is currently unable to work.

admin_accounts_affected.description: How many of the affected accounts are administrators. Count only — never which. Failed attempts against an admin account are a different signal from failed attempts against an author.

last_failure_at.description: Unix timestamp of the most recent failure, or absent if there has been none in the window.
